rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an contains cosmological knowledge in descriptions of the heavens, earth, and creatures of upper and lower worlds.
rows.anchor: وأما الهيئة ففي تضاعيف سوره من الآيات التي ذكر فيها ملكوت السموات والأرض وما بث في العالم العلوي والسفلي من المخلوقات

words: انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an includes material relevant to geometry, illustrated by the shade with three branches.
rows.anchor: وأما الهندسة ففي قوله ﴿ انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب ﴾ الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an contains dialectical tools—proofs, premises, conclusions, counterargument—and Abraham's disputation with Nimrod and his people.
rows.anchor: وأما الجدل فقد حوت آياته من البراهين والمقدمات والنتائج والقول بالموجب والمعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the opening letters encode durations for earlier peoples, this community, and the world's past and remaining time, through multiplied years and days.
rows.anchor: وأما الجبر والمقابلة فقد قيل إن أوائل السور فيها ذكر مدد وأعوام وأيام لتواريخ أمم سالفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interpreted “a remnant of knowledge” as astrology or divination (al-najāmah).
rows.anchor: وأما النجامة ففي قوله ﴿ أو أثارة من علم ﴾ فقد فسره بذلك ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an mentions essential crafts and tools: sewing, smithing, building, shipbuilding, spinning, weaving, farming, hunting, diving, jewelry, glass and pottery work, navigation, writing, breadmaking, cooking, washing, laundering, and butchery.
rows.anchor: وفيه أصول الصنائع وأسماء الآلات التي تدعو الضرورة إليها كالخياطة

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama says the initial descent to the lowest heaven magnified the Qur'an and the Prophet, proclaiming the final scripture for the noblest community.
rows.anchor: الأول قيل السر في إنزاله جملة إلى السماء تفخيم أمره وأمر من نزل عليه

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama says gradual revelation suited unfolding events, while the Qur'an was honored with both complete initial descent and piecemeal delivery.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن الحكمة الإلهية اقتضت وصوله إليهم منجما بحسب الوقائع لهبط به إلى الأرض جملة

rows.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi likens the descent to God delivering the community its share of mercy through Muhammad, with the Qur'an placed at the lowest heaven before Gabriel brought revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكيم الترمذي أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة إلى سماء الدنيا تسليما منه للأمة

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhawi says the descent honored humanity before angels, displayed divine care, and paralleled Moses' complete revelation while distinguishing Muhammad through gradual delivery for memorization.
rows.anchor: وقال السخاوي في جمال القراء في نزوله إلى السماء جملة تكريم بني آدم وتعظيم شأنهم عند الملائكة

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama says the wording can mean God decreed in primordial time that the Qur'an be sent down on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون معنى الكلام إنا حكمنا بإنزاله في ليلة القدر وقضيناه وقدرناه في الأزل

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama's second reading takes the past tense prospectively: God will send the Qur'an down all at once on the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن لفظه لفظ الماضي ومعناه الاستقبال أي ينزله جملة في ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that the challenge concerned God's eternal speech itself, since humans cannot perceive or be challenged by what is inaccessible.
rows.anchor: فزعم قوم أن التحدي وقع بالكلام القديم الذي صفة الذات وأن العرب كلفت في ذلك ما لا يطاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority view preferred by the author is that the challenge concerned Qur'anic words that indicate the eternal speech.
rows.anchor: والصواب ما قاله الجمهور أنه وقع بالدال على القديم وهو الألفاظ

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam held that inimitability is ṣarfah: God diverted the Arabs and stripped their minds though they could otherwise have matched the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ثم زعم النظام أن إعجازه بالصرفة أي أن الله صرف العرب عن معارضته وسلب عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge presumes opponents retain their ability; otherwise their gathering to meet it would be pointless, like gathering the dead.
rows.anchor: فإنه يدل على عجزهم مع بقاء قدرتهم ولو سلبوا القدرة لم يبق لهم فائدة لإجتماعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consensus attributes inimitability to the Qur'an, so ṣarfah wrongly makes God the miracle while leaving no miraculous quality in the text.
rows.anchor: مع أن الإجماع منعقد على إضافة الإعجاز إلى القرآن فكيف يكون معجزا وليس فيه صفة إعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarfah would make the Qur'an cease to be miraculous after the challenge period, contradicting consensus that the Qur'an remains the Prophet's supreme miracle.
rows.anchor: فيلزم من القول بالصرفة زوال الإعجاز بزوال زمان التحدي وخلو القرآن من الإعجاز

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr argues that if composition were possible and only divine prevention stopped it, the prevention, not the Qur'an's speech, would be miraculous.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر ومما يبطل القول بالصرفة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: The author dismisses claims that everyone could compose a match but lacked knowledge of its arrangement, or that later generations remain able to do so.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بأعجب من قول فريق منهم إن الكل قادرون على الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the Qur'an's miraculous quality lies in reports of future unseen events outside the Arabs' knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم وجه إعجازه ما فيه من الإخبار عن الغيوب المستقبلة ولم يكن ذلك من شأن العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an mentions trade, dyeing, stone carving, measures and weights, throwing, tools, foods, drinks, marriage, and events past or future.
rows.anchor: والبيع والشراء في آيات

words: ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The catalog of crafts and created things illustrates the comprehensive sense of “We have neglected nothing in the Book.”
rows.anchor: وجميع ما وقع ويقع في الكائنات ما يحقق معنى قوله

rows.speaker: ابن سراقة
rows.claim: Ibn Suraqa counts arithmetic operations and relations among the Qur'an's miraculous signs: an uneducated Prophet could not have learned them from philosophers or geometers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سراقة من بعض وجوه إعجاز القرآن ما ذكر الله فيه من أعداد الحساب والجمع والقسمة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says the final scripture gathers the fruit of earlier scriptures, whose laws were partly superseded and partly completed by Muhammad's law.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب إن الله تعالى كما جعل نبوة النبيين نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مختتمة

words: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام
rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says the Qur'an's small size contains meaning so vast that human minds cannot enumerate it and worldly instruments cannot exhaust it.
rows.anchor: وجعل من معجزة هذا الكتاب أنه مع قلة الحجم متضمن للمعنى الجم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib likens the Qur'an's guidance to moonlight visible from every direction and sunlight spreading across the lands.
rows.anchor: فهو وإن كان لا يخلو للناظر فيه من نور ما يريه ونفع ما يوليه

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زياد بن أنعم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abu Nu'aym and others says Moses was told Ahmad's book among scriptures resembles milk in a vessel, yielding its cream when churned.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم وغيره عن عبد الرحمن بن زياد بن أنعم قال قيل لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet identified the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage as the Day of Sacrifice; Ibn Umar is cited in support.
rows.anchor: أخرج الترمذي عن علي قال سألت رسول الله

rows.speaker: المسور بن مخرمة
rows.claim: Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama reports the Prophet identifying the Day of Arafah as the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage, an alternative to the Day of Sacrifice.
rows.anchor: عن المسور بن مخرمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( يوم عرفة هذا يوم الحج الأكبر

words: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله
rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet's instruction to regard habitual mosque attendees as believers, citing the verse about maintaining God's mosques.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والترمذي وابن حبان والحاكم عن أبي سعيد قال

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Imran ibn Husayn and Abu Hurayra describes the believer's pearl palace with jewel-built rooms, furnishings, food, and attendants, and renewed strength each morning.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المبارك في الزهد والطبراني والبيهقي في البعث عن عمران بن الحصين وأبي هريرة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: When two men disputed whether the mosque founded on piety was the Prophet's mosque or Quba, the Prophet said it was his; Ahmad gives parallels from Sahl ibn Sa'd and Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وغيره عن أبي سعيد قال اختلف رجلان في المسجد الذي أسس على التقوى

rows.speaker: عويم بن ساعدة الأنصاري
rows.claim: The Prophet praised Quba's purification; its people said they used water after relieving themselves, and he told them to keep doing so.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وابن ماجه وابن خزيمة عن عويم بن ساعدة الأنصاري أن النبي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet explaining that “the travelers” are those who fast.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد can generalize over rational beings, whether many or few.
rows.anchor: فالأول لاستغراق جنس الناطقين ويتناول الكثير والقليل ولذلك صح أن يقال ما من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد occurs in compound numerals with tens, such as eleven and twenty-one.
rows.anchor: الأول المستعمل في العدد مع العشرات نحو أحد عشر أحد وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When annexed, أحد can mean “the first/one of the two,” as in the prisoner's dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: والثاني المستعمل مضافا إليه بمعنى الأول نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an absolute adjective, أحد is restricted to God's description; the related form وحد can be used of others.
rows.anchor: والثالث المستعمل وصفا مطلقا ويختص بوصف الله تعالى نحو

words: ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة
rows.speaker: جعفر بن شمس الخلافة
rows.claim: Ja'far lists this Qur'anic clause among expressions used proverbially (irsāl al-mathal).
rows.anchor: عقد جعفر بن شمس الخلافة في كتاب الآداب بابا في ألفاظ من القرآن جارية مجرى المثل

words: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah 11:44 exemplifies حسن النسق: clauses follow the sequence of water receding, rain stopping, water disappearing, the decree, the ark settling, then a curse; only wrongdoers deserved drowning.
rows.anchor: فإن جمله معطوف بعضها على بعضها بواو النسق على الترتيب الذي تقتضيه البلاغة

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An unnamed view says the Qur'an uses abrupt transitions, the Arabs' way of moving to an unrelated topic.
rows.anchor: وقال إن القرآن إنما ورد على الاقتضاب الذي هو طريقة العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that criticism, saying the Qur'an contains astonishing transitions that bewilder the intellect.
rows.anchor: وليس كما قال ففيه من التخلصات العجيبة ما يحير العقول

words: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'raf moves from earlier peoples and Moses' companions and prayer to God's answer, then to Muhammad's merits and followers.
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى سورة الأعراف كيف ذكر فيها الأنبياء والقرون الماضية والأمم السالفة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some classify the al-A'raf passage as istitrād, not takhallus, because it returns to Moses' story.
rows.anchor: قيل وبهذا يظهر أن ما في سورتي الأعراف والشعراء من باب الاستطراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Shu'ara, Abraham's prayer shifts to the Resurrection and the Day when wealth and children do not benefit.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة الشعراء حكى قول إبراهيم

words: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some classify al-Shu'ara as istitrād because the discourse returns afterward to prophets and earlier communities.
rows.anchor: وفي الشعراء إلى ذكر الأنبياء والأمم

words: فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Kahf, Dhul-Qarnayn's account of the barrier's collapse leads to the portents, resurrection, and fates of unbelievers and believers.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة الكهف حكى قول ذي القرنين في السد بعد دكه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Takhallus leaves the previous topic completely; istitrād briefly visits a side topic and returns as if it arose incidentally.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم الفرق بين التخلص والاستطراد أنك في التخلص تركت ما كنت فيه بالكلية

words: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related transition refreshes listeners by moving from prophets to Paradise and its people, then to Hell and its people.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا القرآن نوع من الذكر لما انتهى ذكر الأنبياء وهو نوع من التنزيل

rows.speaker: الحزاني
rows.claim: Al-Hazani maps the seven letters onto three perfected domains—worldly life, religion, and the afterlife—each with paired action and restraint, yielding six letters.
rows.anchor: وقال الحزاني في معنى حديث

rows.speaker: الحزاني
rows.claim: He assigns worldly benefit to halal and haram, afterlife benefit to command and prohibition, and religious benefit to clear and ambiguous passages; the latter teaches human limits.
rows.anchor: وقال الحزاني في معنى حديث

rows.speaker: الحزاني
rows.claim: Al-Hazani says the Qur'an completes teachings rooted in earlier scriptures and has a seventh, unpaired letter: the comprehensive parable pointing to the Highest Example.
rows.anchor: وقال الحزاني في معنى حديث

rows.speaker: الحزاني
rows.claim: He presents Muhammad as the final, comprehensive prophet and links the Qur'an's completion to the mission to perfect noble character and a prayer for well-being in faith, life, and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الحزاني في معنى حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean preserving or remembering what is in the scripture.
rows.anchor: والحفظ ﴿ واذكروا ما فيه ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean obedience and its reward.
rows.anchor: والطاعة والجزاء ﴿ فاذكروني أذكركم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer to the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: والصلوات الخمس ﴿ فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean admonition or reminder.
rows.anchor: والعظة ﴿ فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به ﴾

words: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean explanatory message or clarification.
rows.anchor: والبيان ﴿ أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Joseph's request, dhikr means speaking to the king or telling him Joseph's situation.
rows.anchor: والحديث ﴿ اذكرني عند ربك ﴾ أي حدثه بحالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والقرآن ﴿ ومن أعرض عن ذكري ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer to the Torah.
rows.anchor: والتوراة ﴿ فاسألوا أهل الذكر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean a report or account.
rows.anchor: والخبر ﴿ سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean honor or renown.
rows.anchor: والشرف ﴿ وإنه لذكر لك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean disparagement or criticism.
rows.anchor: والعيب ﴿ أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer to the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: واللوح المحفوظ ﴿ من بعد الذكر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean praise or remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: والثناء ﴿ وذكر الله كثيرا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can mean revelation.
rows.anchor: والوحي ﴿ فالتاليات ذكرا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can designate the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والرسول ﴿ ذكرا رسولا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer to ritual prayer.
rows.anchor: والصلاة ﴿ ولذكر الله أكبر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer specifically to Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الجمعة ﴿ فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can refer specifically to the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وصلاة العصر ﴿ عن ذكر ربي ﴾

words: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean worship.
rows.anchor: 1 العبادة ﴿ ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean seeking help.
rows.anchor: 2 والاستعانة ﴿ وادعوا شهداءكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean asking or supplication.
rows.anchor: 3 والسؤال ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean speech or utterance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean calling or summoning.
rows.anchor: 5 والنداء ﴿ يوم يدعوكم ﴾

words: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du'a can mean naming or addressing someone.
rows.anchor: 6 والتسمية ﴿ لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan can mean chastity.
rows.anchor: 1 العفة ﴿ والذين يرمون المحصنات ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan can mean marriage.
rows.anchor: 2 والتزوج ﴿ فإذا أحصن ﴾

words: نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan can mean free status, contrasted with enslaved women.
rows.anchor: 3 والحرية ﴿ نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ﴾

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One derivation treats Adam as a diptote formed from أدمة, a complexion quality.
rows.anchor: 1 - آدم أبو البشر ذكر قوم أنه

rows.speaker: الجواليقي
rows.claim: Al-Jawaliqi says all prophetic names are foreign except Adam, Salih, Shu'ayb, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الجواليقي أسماء الأنبياء كلها أعجمية إلا أربعة آدم وصالح وشعيب ومحمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam was named because he was created from the surface soil of the earth.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق أبي الضحى عن ابن عباس قال إنما سمى آدم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others derive Adam from Syriac Ādam, with the second alif omitted in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم هو اسم سرياني أصله

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi says the Hebrew word for soil is ādam and Adam was named from it.
rows.anchor: وقال الثعلبي التراب بالعبرانية آدام فسمى آدم به

rows.speaker: ابن أبي خيثمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Khaythama gives Adam's lifespan as 960 years.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي خيثمة عاش تسعمائة سنة وستين سنة

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says historical books commonly report Adam lived one thousand years.
rows.anchor: وقال النووي في تهذيبه اشتهر في كتب التواريخ أنه عاش ألف سنة

rows.speaker: الجواليقي
rows.claim: Al-Jawaliqi calls Noah a foreign name Arabized into Arabic; al-Kirmani gives its Syriac meaning as “settled,” with a version reading “grateful.”
rows.anchor: قال الجواليقي أعجمي معرب زاد الكرماني ومعناه بالسريانية

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim says Noah was named for weeping over himself, gives his name as Abd al-Ghaffar, and reports most Companions placed Noah before Idris.
rows.anchor: وقال الحاكم في المستدرك إنما سمى نوحا لكثرة بكائه على نفسه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: An alternative genealogy identifies Noah as son of Lamak, through Methuselah and Enoch (Idris).
rows.anchor: وقال غيره هو نوح بن لمك بفتح اللام وسكون الميم بعدها كاف

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet naming Adam the first prophet and Noah the next, with twenty qarn between them.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبراني عن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله من أول الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives ten generations as the interval between Adam and Noah, differing from Abu Dharr's twenty qarn.
rows.anchor: وفي المستدرك عن ابن عباس قال كان بين آدم ونوح عشرة قرون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A marfu' report from Ibn Abbas says Noah was commissioned at forty, preached for 950 years, and lived sixty years after the Flood until people multiplied.
rows.anchor: وفيه عنه مرفوعا ( بعث الله نوحا لأربعين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says Noah was born 126 years after Adam's death.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن جرير أن مولد نوح كان بعد وفاة آدم

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says Noah was the longest-lived of the prophets.
rows.anchor: وفي التهذيب للنووي أنه أطول الأنبياء عمرا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Idris lived before Noah.
rows.anchor: 3 - إدريس قيل إنه قبل نوح

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Idris was the first descendant of Adam granted prophethood and identifies him as Enoch in Adam's line.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق كان إدريس أول بني آدم أعطي النبوة وهو أخنوخ بن يرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in the king's question is emphatic or strengthening, reinforcing a weak or delayed governing element.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد وهي الزائدة أو المقوية للعامل الضعيف لفرعية أو تأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis calls the lām a particle of consequence: enmity was the outcome, not the captors' purpose; some call this figurative causation.
rows.anchor: والصيرورة وتسمى لام العاقبة نحو

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a literal purposive reading, supplying an omitted noun: they took Moses for fear he would become an enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان الذي عندي أنها للتعليل حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can emphasize or strengthen a weak or delayed governing element, illustrated by the king's question.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد وهي الزائدة أو المقوية للعامل الضعيف لفرعية أو تأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicative lām marks the person or thing to which a preceding expression refers or is explained.
rows.anchor: والتبيين للفاعل أو المفعول نحو

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufan grammarians say the purposive lām itself governs the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: والناصبة هي لام التعليل وادعى الكوفيون نصبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians analyze an implicit أن as subjunctive and governed in the genitive after the lām.
rows.anchor: وقال غيرهم بأن مقدرة في محل جر باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request lām is normally kasra but opened by Sulaym; after wāw and fā it is more often quiescent, and can follow thumma.
rows.anchor: والجازمة وهي لام الطلب وحركتها الكسر وسليم تفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request lām occurs in commands and supplications and can also express reported statements, future action, or threats.
rows.anchor: وسواء كان الطلب أمرا نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jussive lām occurs most often with third-person verbs, rarely with second-person verbs, and least often with first-person verbs.
rows.anchor: وجزمها فعل الغائب كثير نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “a bow's length,” complements of kāna's subject and predicate are omitted; the sense is that the distance of approach equaled a bow's length.
rows.anchor: أي فكان مقدار مسافة قربه مثل قاب قوسين فحذف ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objects of ظنّ are omitted; the intended sense is “you claimed them to be My partners.”
rows.anchor: حذف مفعولي باب ظن ﴿ أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preposition and its object are omitted: they mixed righteous work with bad work, and bad work with righteous work.
rows.anchor: حذف الجار مع المجرور ﴿ خلطوا عملا صالحا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinator and its coordinated element can be omitted; this type was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: حذف العاطف مع المعطوف تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After an imperative, the conditional particle and clause may be omitted: “follow me” means “if you follow me, God will love you.”
rows.anchor: حذف حرف الشرط وفعله يطرد بعد الطلب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the phrase conditionally: if they made a covenant with God, He will not break it.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه الزمخشري ﴿ فلن يخلف الله عهده ﴾ أي إن اتخذتم

words: فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل
rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan analyzes an omitted condition: if they believed what was revealed, why did they previously kill God's prophets?
rows.anchor: وجعل منه أبو حيان ﴿ فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apodosis may be omitted; here the completion is “then do so.”
rows.anchor: حذف جواب الشرط ﴿ فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted result of being told to beware is “they turned away,” as the following text indicates.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون ﴾ أي أعرضوا بدليل ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted response to “when you are reminded” is that they took it as an evil omen.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أئن ذكرتم ﴾ أي تطيرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted apodosis is that God's words would be exhausted if the sea were replenished with its like as ink.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولو جئنا بمثله مددا ﴾ أي لنفذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted result is that one would see a dreadful scene if the criminals were seen with bowed heads.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رؤوسهم ﴾ أي لرأيت أمرا فظيعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted result is that God would have punished them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله رؤوف رحيم ﴾ أي لعذبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted result is that Moses' mother would have disclosed her grief.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها ﴾ أي لأبدت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted result is that the believers would have been allowed to overcome Mecca's people if unknown believers had not been there.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطؤوهم ﴾ أي لسلطكم على أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath before “I will punish him severely” is omitted; the implied oath is “By God.”
rows.anchor: حذف جملة القسم ﴿ لأعذبنه عذابا شديدا ﴾ أي والله حذف جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to the oath by the angels is understood as “you will surely be resurrected.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ والنازعات غرقا ﴾ الآيات أي لتبعثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to the oath by the Qur'an is “it is indeed miraculous.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ ص والقرآن ذي الذكر ﴾ أي إنه لمعجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to the oath is “the matter is not as they claim.”
rows.anchor: ﴿ ق والقرآن المجيد ﴾ أي ما الأمر كما زعموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sentence giving the cause of the stated action is omitted; the intended sense is “He did what He did.”
rows.anchor: حذف جملة مسببة عن المذكور نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many clauses are omitted after the cupbearer's request: they sent him to Joseph to ask about the dream, and he went and addressed Joseph as truthful one.
rows.anchor: حذف جمل كثيرة نحو
